instruction: I need to apply italic formatting to all uppercase text in my document for stylistic emphasis. Could you help me accomplish this?

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Applies italic formatting to all uppercase text. Verified by checking all uppercase text runs have italic formatting.

llm_judge_reasons: Critical edge case error: metric returns 0.0 when uppercase_count==0, but should return 1.0 (vacuously true - if no uppercase text exists, all uppercase text is trivially italic)

Semantic granularity issue: getter checks if entire run is uppercase (text.isupper()), not individual uppercase characters. A run like 'ABC123' would be missed even though it contains uppercase letters
Run-level verification may not align with instruction intent: user may apply italic to uppercase words/characters differently than how they're grouped into runs, causing false negatives
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Fix metric logic: return 1.0 when uppercase_count==0 (empty case should pass)
Consider character-level analysis: iterate through each character in runs and check if uppercase characters have italic formatting, rather than checking if entire runs are uppercase
Add edge case handling for mixed-case runs containing uppercase letters that should be italic
